rows.q: Teach me what a Statement of Applicability is.
rows.answer:
A Statement of Applicability (SoA) is a key document in ISO/IEC 27001:2022 that lists all 93 controls from Annex A and states, for each one, whether it applies to your organization’s ISMS, why it applies or does not apply, and whether it is currently implemented. It is required by clause 6.1.3 d) and serves as the link between your risk assessment and the controls you choose to treat those risks. The SoA also includes a Risk Treatment Plan (clause 6.1.3 e) to schedule implementation of any controls that are applicable but not yet in place, and by approving it, risk owners formally accept the residual risks (clause 6.1.3 f).

An auditor will check that the SoA exists, is approved, and contains a clear justification for each control’s applicability status. They will verify that the implementation status matches what is actually in place and that any controls marked as “not yet implemented” have a corresponding plan in the Risk Treatment Plan. Evidence includes the SoA document itself, approval records, and links to risk treatment actions.

In your project, the SoA was prepared on 18/10/2026 [S5] and covers all 93 Annex A controls, with 93 applicable and 0 excluded [S4]. Of these, 84 are implemented and 9 are not yet implemented and are tracked in the Risk Treatment Plan [S4]. Your SoA is maintained by the CISO [S7] and is stored with version control [S7]. You can see examples of how controls are justified in your SoA entries—for instance, A.6.5 and A.6.6 are marked applicable because they treat specific risks (R-008 and R-021) [F6, F7]. This shows your SoA is actively used to link risk treatment to control selection, as required.

rows.q: Explain clause 9.2 and how our project covers it.
rows.answer:
Clause 9.2 of ISO/IEC 27001:2022 requires that an organization conduct internal audits at planned intervals to verify whether the ISMS conforms to its own requirements and to the standard, and that the audit programme is effectively implemented. The purpose is to detect nonconformities, assess the effectiveness of controls, and provide input for management review and continual improvement. An auditor checks that an audit programme exists (defining scope, frequency, methods, responsibilities), that auditors are independent and competent, that audit criteria are clearly referenced (e.g., ISMS policies, procedures, the standard), that findings are documented with evidence, and that results are reported to relevant management and followed up. Evidence includes an approved audit schedule, audit checklists, audit reports with findings and auditor signatures, records of auditor training, and a corrective action register tracking follow-up.

Your project covers clause 9.2 through the following:
- The "Internal Audit Procedure" document (version 1.0, approved 2026-10-18) establishes the audit programme, defines responsibilities, and outlines how audits are conducted and reported [F12].
- The "Internal Audit Report" (version 1.0, approved 2026-10-18) provides evidence of audit execution, including findings and conclusions [F11].
- The procedure references ISO/IEC 27001 clause 9.2 and ISO 19011 as basis [S1], and specifies that audit records (programme, checklists, reports) are retained in APTISO for at least three years [S4].
- The procedure applies to the entire ISMS scope and is intended for top management and ISMS personnel [S6].

However, as the project lead, you should note that Phase 5 (ISMS Maintenance & Certification Cycle) has not started [F1], meaning the internal audit programme may not yet be fully operationalized for ongoing cycles. The next step is to ensure the audit programme is activated and audits are conducted at planned intervals as part of ISMS maintenance, especially since two internal audit nonconformities from "Management review 16/10/2026" remain open and are due for closure by 2026-12-31 [data name="person"]. You should verify that audit planning, auditor independence, and follow-up on nonconformities are being addressed in line with the procedure.

rows.q: What does control A.8.13 require?
rows.answer: Control A.8.13 requires that backup copies of information, software, and systems are maintained and regularly tested to ensure recoverability. This includes defining backup frequency, scope, retention periods, securing backup storage (segregated from production), and verifying that recovery time objectives (RTO) and recovery point objectives (RPO) are met. An auditor checks for a backup policy, evidence of regular backups, test restore reports, and secure backup storage configuration. Common pitfalls include performing backups without testing restores or storing backups in the same location as primary systems. [S2]

rows.q: What is the difference between a nonconformity and an observation in an audit?
rows.answer: A nonconformity is a failure to meet a requirement of ISO/IEC 27001:2022, a policy, or a procedure—such as missing training records or an overdue access review—while an observation is a note about something that is not a nonconformity but could be improved, like objectives only having a baseline measurement or no restore test performed yet. Observations do not indicate non-compliance but highlight opportunities for continual improvement [S4][S6][S8]. In your internal audit report, NC-003 (competence) and NC-004 (access rights) are minor nonconformities, while the two observations relate to unmeasured objectives and missing restore tests [S8]. Your Procedure for Nonconformities and Corrective Actions requires nonconformities to be recorded, analysed, and corrected to prevent recurrence, with effectiveness reviewed [S2][S3][S5][S7]. Observations, though not requiring corrective action, should still be tracked and considered in management review for improvement [S6]. As project lead, you should ensure the two nonconformities are closed and the first backup restore test is run by 2026-12-31, as decided in your last management review [data name="person"].

rows.q: Explain clause 6.1.2 risk assessment in simple words.
rows.answer:
Clause 6.1.2 of ISO/IEC 27001:2022 requires the organization to define and apply a process for identifying information security risks. This means systematically finding out what could go wrong with information assets (like data leaks, system failures, or unauthorized access), how likely it is to happen, and what the impact would be if it did. The goal is to understand the level of risk so that decisions can be made about what needs to be treated.

An auditor will check whether the organization has a documented risk assessment process, whether it has been applied to identify risks across the ISMS scope, and whether the results are recorded (e.g., in a risk register or risk assessment report). Evidence includes the risk assessment methodology, completed risk assessment tables, and records showing that risk owners were involved.

Your project has a documented "Risk Assessment and Risk Treatment Methodology" (approved since 2026-10-18) that covers clause 6.1.2 [F2], and a "Risk Assessment and Treatment Report" that records the results [F4]. This shows the risk assessment process is defined and applied, meeting the core requirement of 6.1.2. However, note that the annual risk review (due 2027-10-18) is still pending as part of the ISMS maintenance cycle [F1], which is needed to keep the risk assessment up to date.

The control in your Statement of Applicability that covers backup is **A.8.13 Information backup**, not A.12.3.1 (which is from the 2013 version of the standard and not used in ISO/IEC 27001:2022).  

Your SoA shows that A.8.13 is applicable, with implementation status **PLANNED**, and it is intended to treat risks R-001 and R-005. The method is defined in the Backup policy, with Sarra Mansouri as the responsible owner and a deadline of 2026-12-15 [F13].  

The Backup policy document (version 1.0, approved 2026-10-18) covers A.8.13 [F20], and both the IT Security Policy [F23] and the Backup policy itself reference this control for backup arrangements [S3][S4].  

Note: A.12.3.1 does not exist in ISO/IEC 27001:2022. The equivalent control for backup in the 2022 version is **A.8.13 Information backup**. If you saw A.12.3.1 in older documents, it should be updated to reflect the 2022 structure.  

Next step: Ensure the backup restore test is performed (as per your management review action due 2026-12-31) to move A.8.13 from PLANNED to IMPLEMENTED.
